simple.meaning: מָשַׁשׁ (mâshash) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to feel of ; by implication, to grope.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Job, beginning at Genesis 27:12. Its contexts include family, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָשַׁשׁ (H4959).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָשַׁשׁ (mâshash) / H4959 is traced through Genesis 27:12, Genesis 27:22, Genesis 31:34, Genesis 31:37 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to feel of ; by implication, to grope

firstOccurrence.englishText: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.”

timeline.evidenceText: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
Jacob went near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.
Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.”
You will grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways. You will only be oppressed and robbed always, and there will be no one to save you.
You will grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways. You will only be oppressed and robbed always, and there will be no one to save you.
They meet with darkness in the day time,
They grope in the dark without light.

definitions.short: to feel of ; by implication, to grope
definitions.full: H4959. mashash [ מָשַׁשׁ ] verb feel, grope (Late Hebrew id. Pi`el; Arabic feel ; Ethiopic Di 166 ; Aramaic , מְשַׁשׁ Pa`el, Palpel — see also ימשׁ , II. מושׁ ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine singular suffix יְמֻשֵּׁנִי Gen 27:12 perhaps my father will feel me ; וַיְמֻשֵּׁהוּ 27:22 and he felt of him (both J). Pi`el Perfect 2masculine singular מִשַּׁשְׁתָּ ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יְמַשֵּׁשׁ Deut 28:29 , וַיְמַשֵּׁשׁ Gen 31:34 ; 3 masculine plural יִמַשְׁשׁוּ Job 5:4 ; 12:25 ; Participle מְמַשֵּׁשׁ Deut 28:29 ; — feel over or through, grope: — 1 ׳וַיְמ אֶתכָּֿלהָֿאֹהֶל לָבָּן Gen 31:24 and Laban felt through the whole tent (i.e. searched it); so (object כֵּלַי ) 31:37 thou hast felt through all my possessions (or baggage; both E). 2 grope , of blind Deut 28:29 b (in simile), periphrase conjectural, מְמַשֵּׁשׁ וְהָיִיתָ 28:29 a and thou shalt become one that gropes at noonday (figurative of judicial blindness); compare Job 5:14 ; 12:25 . Hiph`il Imperfect חשֶׁךְ וְיָמֵשׁ Exod 10:21 that one may feel (the) darkness ; read also Imperative suffix הֲמִשֵׁנִי (for והימשׁני , see ימשׁ , p. 413 above) Judg 16:26 and let me touch the pillars (2 accusative) מִשְׁתֶּה see שׁתה . מֵת see מות . p 559, 1059
